purpose: WIN-260 (M2.5). The canonical failure taxonomy: every SCREAMING_SNAKE code any of the 17 bounded contexts mints, the ErrorCategory it carries, and the HTTP status a transport answers with. M0.4 section 2 makes a code immutable within a major and the kernel's vo/error.ts says the code-to-status table belongs to WIN-260; this is that table. It is DATA rather than a derivation so that scripts/error-taxonomy.mjs can join it to three things it does not control - the 17 contexts' mint sites, apps/core-api/src/transports/error-status.ts, and the kernel's own ErrorCategory union - and fail when any two disagree.
procedure: Adding a code: mint it in the owning context, run `pnpm generate:error-taxonomy`, then CHOOSE its status. The generator writes a new code with status null on purpose - a generator that invented the status would make rule E9 unfalsifiable. Removing a code: delete the mint site and regenerate; a stale entry fails E2. Changing a status: change apps/core-api/src/transports/error-status.ts and regenerate, so the two files move together.

rules.E1: every minted code has an entry here
rules.E2: every entry here names a code some context mints
rules.E3: the category here matches the category at the mint site
rules.E4: the status here matches what apps/core-api/src/transports/error-status.ts resolves
rules.E5: that module's category table covers the kernel ErrorCategory union exactly
rules.E6: every function that raises one code twice with identical arguments is registered in uniformGuards, with the reason the answers must be indistinguishable
rules.E7: every uniformGuards entry still describes a live guard
rules.E8: every STATUS_OVERRIDES entry names a code some context mints
rules.E9: every entry carries a status, and one its category permits
rules.E10: every entry records the contexts that mint the code

uniformity: A repeated raise is not by itself a defect. `admitBudget` refuses six different fields under COST_BUDGET_INVALID and attaches a distinct FieldViolation to each, so the guards are distinguishable at runtime even though the code is shared. What is a defect is a repeated raise with IDENTICAL arguments, because nothing then separates the two answers - that is how four facts hid behind one IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT in jobs, and how two defects hid behind one code in privacy and in identity-access. Some identical repeats are nevertheless REQUIRED: identity-access answers one INVALID_MFA_CODE for every way a second factor can fail, precisely so a caller cannot learn which guess got closer. Those are the entries below, each with the reason.

uniformGuards.reason: One store-unreachable refusal, raised from each command of the same factory. The guards report the SAME fact - this PostgreSQL client could not answer - and an operator's next move is identical whichever command hit it. Distinguishing them would name the command, which the log line already carries.

The repository half of the same fact, uniform for the same reason: every command of this factory reports one unreachable store, and the command that hit it travels in the log line rather than in the code.
The same store-unreachable refusal inside the credential store's own factory. Two commands, one incident, one operator action.

Four cache commands - get, set, delete and the prefix sweep - each reporting that this Redis connection could not answer. Deliberately uniform: the caller falls through to the canonical store in every case, so which command failed is a log field rather than a contract.

Absent and visible-but-not-yours answer identically on purpose. Telling them apart would make the endpoint an existence oracle for another actor's macro ids; the file's own header says collapsing them 'would either leak or mislead'.

The same existence-oracle defence as requireVisible(), repeated on the write path: the row is missing, or it is there and this actor may not see it. Distinguishing them would let a caller enumerate macro ids it has no access to.

'Not refreshing at all' and 'refreshing but not yet stale' are one instruction to the caller — do not reclaim this lease — and the error already carries refreshState in details, which is the field that separates them for an operator.

A cap that vanished between the read and the conditional write was already gone. The extraction source returns false there and the surface renders the same 404, so the write-race is deliberately spelled as the error the read path would have produced.

A crossing with no event row and a crossing whose budget row is gone are the same fact to a delivery worker: this crossing can no longer be described. Naming the missing budget separately would disclose that a budget id existed.

Both raises interpolate the offending value into the message and pass it in details, so the two guards — not an integer, and out of range — are distinguishable in the payload even though the constructor call is identical.
The opening shape guard and the default branch both mean 'this is not one of the four delivery types', and both quote the same list of four. They are the same fact reached from two directions.
'No revision' and 'a revision that is not the one asked for' are one answer: the requested revision does not exist. The requested number is in details, which is what an operator reads.
The turn is missing, or it belongs to another end user. Separating them would let one end user probe another's turn ids by the difference in the reply.
The thread is missing, or it belongs to another agent. The same cross-tenant probing defence as resolveTarget(): a distinct code would confirm the thread exists.
Both raises carry the offending minimum and maximum, so a non-integer scale and an inverted one are told apart by the values in the error rather than by the code.
A rating is +1 or -1. 'Not an integer' and 'an integer that is not one of the two' are one fact — this is not a rating — and the offending value travels in the error.
Too few segments and an empty segment are both 'this rule identity does not parse', and both carry the whole rule string, which is what a producer needs to fix it.
REQUIRED to be uniform. 'There is no pending enrolment' and 'those six digits are wrong' must be one answer, or the reply tells an attacker whether an enrolment is in flight for this account.

REQUIRED to be uniform. Already impersonating, not a platform operator, and 'no such target or the target is disabled' must be indistinguishable, or the reply becomes an account-existence and account-state oracle for anyone holding an operator session.
REQUIRED to be uniform, for the same reason as startImpersonation(): every way a stop can be refused answers identically so the refusal discloses nothing about the session it was aimed at.

REQUIRED to be uniform. A wrong recovery code and no second factor supplied at all answer identically; the catalogue's own note is that distinguishing the ways a second factor fails 'tells a caller which guess got closer'.

REQUIRED to be uniform. No enrolled secret, wrong digits, and a counter another request advanced first are one answer by design — the last is a replay, and naming it would confirm that the code presented was otherwise correct.

Both raises name the requested agent and say it is not bound here; they are the same denial reached with and without an acting agent. The message and the agent id in the error are what an operator reads.
'The model string yields no lookup key' and 'no rate card matches any key at this instant' are one fact to a caller pricing a turn: this model cannot be priced now. Both carry the model.

REQUIRED to be uniform. The root key is reported absent by the ring, or the handle for it cannot be taken. Both are 'root_key_absent' deliberately: a caller must not learn from a reply which key versions the ring is holding.

The seal and open halves of one in-memory cipher both refuse a missing root key version, identically, because the real adapter has one answer for it. Two codes here would be two codes the vendor cipher cannot produce.

An in-memory stand-in for the store: three methods report 'credential_not_found' for a row that is not in its map. The real repository answers one code for a missing row and the double must not be finer than the thing it stands in for.

Not installed and installed-but-disabled are one answer on the RUN path: the skill is not runnable here. The install surface is where the two are separated, because there the difference is actionable.

Two closures in one factory — resolveEnvironmentScope and describeTenant — each refuse an unknown environment. They are two readings of one fact, not two guards in one decision; the scan sees one function because the closures share the factory body.

REQUIRED to be uniform. Every gate answers one code so that probing cannot enumerate environments, organizations or roles; which gate refused travels in details.gate, which the catalogue marks log-only. Five raises in two groups: three under 'organization-membership' and two under 'project-membership'.

REQUIRED to be uniform. The invitation is for another address, or the account signing in has no address that matches. Separating them would say which of the two the caller got wrong about an invitation it does not own.
